10 best gift ideas for flight simulator enthusiasts

Flight-simulator enthusiasts can be as particular about their setup as pilots are about cockpit equipment. Start with the simulator, platform, and controls they already use. This shortlist mixes named products to investigate with practical supporting gifts, without claiming hands-on tests or universal compatibility.

By Pilot Gift Guide · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEHow to chooseThe listRelated guides

How to choose

Ask for exact software versions and hardware model numbers before buying. A PC product may not suit a console setup, and similarly named control variants can differ. The best gift improves the recipient’s existing experience rather than requiring a chain of unplanned purchases.

The list

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    Requested simulator aircraft add-on

    An exact wish-list add-on is our first direction for an established simmer. Confirm simulator version, platform, license, and installation requirements before purchase.

  2. 2

    Thrustmaster TCA Sidestick Airbus Edition

    A named control to investigate for someone interested in a sidestick setup. Verify this exact edition’s compatibility rather than assuming every Airbus-branded variant works identically.

    Official source: thrustmaster.com ↗
  3. 3

    Honeycomb Alpha Flight Controls

    A yoke option to discuss with a recipient who wants that control style. Check the exact version, mounting arrangement, and supported setup.

    Official source: flyhoneycomb.com ↗
  4. 4

    Honeycomb Bravo Throttle Quadrant

    Consider this only when a throttle upgrade is on their list. Confirm compatibility and whether the available desk space supports the complete arrangement.

    Official source: flyhoneycomb.com ↗
  5. 5

    X-Plane 12 contribution

    A software option for someone who specifically wants X-Plane. Use the official demo and current requirements to assess their setup before buying a license.

    Official source: x-plane.com ↗
  6. 6

    Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 contribution

    Confirm the desired platform and edition through official information. Do not assume a purchase on one platform fits the recipient’s existing account or equipment.

    Official source: flightsimulator.com ↗
  7. 7

    Compatible desk mount

    A stable, suitable mount can improve an existing setup. Get dimensions and manufacturer compatibility confirmation rather than choosing by appearance alone.

  8. 8

    Control storage solution

    A padded shelf, case, or cabinet can help in a shared room. Measure the actual equipment and avoid putting strain on attached cables.

  9. 9

    Simulator desk notebook

    A simple notebook can hold personal setup notes and virtual-trip ideas. Present it as a hobby accessory, separate from real-world operational references.

  10. 10

    ATC — real airport listening away from the simulator

    Our app: Pilot Gift Guide is produced by the team behind ATC. This is a recommendation of our own product.

    A simulator enthusiast who enjoys radio traffic may also like exploring ATC on an iPhone. It offers live airport audio, maps, transcripts and replay as a separate listening experience. It is not a simulator add-on or a connection to a virtual ATC network; choose it for their curiosity about real airport activity.

    For iPhone with iOS 18 or later. Airport coverage varies. Check current subscription pricing, renewal terms and gift options at ATC.com before paying.

    Explore ATC ↗ · App Store details ↗
